title: The manhood of Christ as the way to the Father's truth and life
english: For the manhood of Christ has become for us the starting point of the fairest ways of righteousness, leading us to better pursuits. It fittingly joins us to the Spirit, guides us into paradise, and restores us to our proper pasture. Therefore Christ said, “I am the way and the truth and the life” (John 14:6). By the name “way” he indicates the covering according to the manhood, which belongs to bodily and visible things; for a way is a portion of earth and a perceptible ground. But the name “truth” and “life” indicates the nature of the Father; for truth is an intelligible thing that falls under neither sight nor touch.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius opens his treatise by presenting the manhood of Christ as the starting point of the fairest paths of righteousness, then interprets Christ's saying 'I am the way and the truth and the life.'
